crime: Every evening, a girl climbed the tree in the courtyard to see over the wall, and {WITCH_NAME} waited at its foot. Whenever the girl came down scraped, {WITCH_NAME} touched the scrapes and took them onto her own skin.
One day at dusk, the girl fell and landed on both hands, breaking both wrists. {WITCH_NAME} took the breaks into her own wrists. The prisoners watched hers swell and bend as the girl's straightened.
Then the girl wrapped {WITCH_NAME}'s palms in strips of rag. "That was the last one," she said. "From now on, I keep my own hurts."
{WITCH_NAME}'s older sister had once closed her fist over her own grazed palm, said, "This one I keep," and left home before winter.
That evening, the prisoners splinted {WITCH_NAME}'s wrists and left her asleep in the medical room.

That night, the girl sat alone at the foot of the tree, wrapping her own palms. {WITCH_NAME} came up behind her, looped a strip of rag around her throat, wound the ends around her splinted forearms and leaned back until the girl was still.
Before lockup, the prisoners found the girl strangled beneath the tree, the strip ringed around her throat.

In the trial court, they ruled {WITCH_NAME} out: wrists broken since dusk could not pull a strip tight. Then her collar slipped, and a prisoner saw four raw nail lines across her throat. The prisoners understood: they were the girl's own claw marks, drawn off her throat as she died.
fields.epitaph: The only hurt left for her to keep was the one she gave.
fields.epithet: Keeper of Hurts Not Her Own
execution: The execution stand raises a giant iron hand, palm up. She kneels shackled in its palm, holding out her own hands. The fingers fold down over her one by one, the thumb last, pressing her into the palm. The hand stays shut as a fist. Nothing inside moves.

magic.name: Kiss It Better
magic.text: She can take the wounds, pain or sickness of anyone she touches into her own body.
